articles.title: Emacs Turns 50
articles.summary: Emacs, the software that revolutionized programming, first ran on the early video terminals at the MIT Artificial Intelligence Laboratory in 1976, but its core concepts were so powerful that it was rewritten for many operating systems in the decades that followed. The first programmers didn't write code at all, but instead physically configured switches, cables, and plugboards, and later punched code onto paper tape that was then loaded into the computer's memory. The software-­sharing community that started around Emacs helped give rise to the modern-day free software movement and the GNU/Linux operating system, and its roots begin with the TECO text editor that Dan Murphy created in 1962 for the pioneering PDP-1 computer at MIT.

This is a serious vulnerability that can allow attackers to intercept and tamper with HTTPS connections, including those to GitHub and other remote servers. To check if your git is affected, run the command git ls-remote https://git-emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/check.git, and if a certificate error is reported, your git is protected. To see an attack end to end, run the command that clones a repository from a test server impersonating GitHub, and if the clone succeeds, you'll see a README.md starting with INTERCEPTED.
